paper.title: Algorithm 831: Modified Bessel Functions of Imaginary Order and Positive Argument
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 30(2), 159-164 (TOMS 831, June 2004)

code.archive: netlib TOMS 831.gz, sha256 5d56edbba35b73c301c3abe6684b47dda84758b4df2dbf8f2f88cbabf49a885a (hashed by scout from the fetched bytes)
code.note: Shell archive (Fortran77): Drivers/wktest.f is PROGRAM WKTEST (check the PROGRAM line). Its last test (line ~154, IFAC=2, scaled functions) loops I=1..1000 step 10 with X=0.95*I and J=1..1000 step 10 with A=0.9*J, computes |X*KIA*LIAP-1 - X*KIAP*LIA| from DKIA/DLIA, and prints WMAX as the last line of Drivers/Res. Src/src.f, airy.f and d1mach.f are the sources. gfortran is not in the scout sandbox.

field: numerics (special functions, Bessel functions of imaginary order)

claim.location: Paper abstract (TOMS 30(2) p.159) and Section 2 (pp.161-162): 'The relative accuracy is better than 10^-13 in the range (0,200] x [-200,200] and close to 10^-12 in (0,1500) x [-1500,1500)'. The Wronskian grid of the driver (X up to 941, |A| up to 892) lies inside the stated (0,1500) x [-1500,1500) range.

reference.file: Fortran77/Drivers/Res (member of 831.gz), last line 'MAXIMUM VALUE OF THE WRONSKIAN CHECK = 6.814548925149211E-13' under 'TEST OF THE WRONSKIAN RELATION FOR DKIA, DLIA' (IFAC=2)

claim.metric: Maximum absolute Wronskian residual |X*K*L'-1 - X*K'*L| (DKIA, DLIA, scaled functions, IFAC=2) over the driver's grid, as printed by WKTEST.
claim.paper_value: Paper: relative accuracy 'close to 10^-12' over (0,1500)x[-1500,1500) and better than 5x10^-13 over (0,500]x[-500,500]. The grid is not inside (0,500]x[-500,500] (|A| reaches 892), so only the 10^-12 scale applies to the whole grid.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The rerun maximum must lie within 1e-13 absolute of the shipped 6.8145e-13, so it is in [5.81e-13, 7.81e-13]. The paper's scale for this grid is 'close to 10^-12', so the rerun must also report whether its maximum is below 1e-12 and say so in its note. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 5 minutes: compile the Fortran 77 sources and run one 100x100 grid.
cost.data_size: None; the driver generates its own grid.
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence in the archive; the rerun should record the licence text.

why: The paper states the accuracy scale of these functions, and the shipped driver computes the Wronskian residual those accuracy statements rest on, so the code has to compute the number.
